---
title: "Comping rhythm: Bossa nova"
subtitle: "For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2
---

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Bossa nova**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

A two-bar pattern. First bar (shown): beat 1, the and of 2 held, beat 3. Second bar: beat 2 and the and of 3.

It belongs in *Bossa nova*. Here it is in the bossa nova style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"compRhythm":"bossa"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-pad.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Charleston

A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-charleston.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Bossa nova, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two bars: beat 1, the and of 2 held, beat 3; then beat 2 and the and of 3. On guitar the thumb plays the bass on 1 and 3 while the fingers play this rhythm.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"compRhythm":"bossa"}},{"label":"Charleston (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"compRhythm":"bossa"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"compRhythm":"bossa"}}]'></div>

## Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7 D7|Gmaj7 Em7|Am7 D7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"compRhythm":"bossa"}}]'></div>

- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Bossa nova](bass-bossa.qmd) (bass line), [Bossa nova](drums-bossa.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in bossa nova:** [Bossa nova](bass-bossa.qmd) (bass line), [Bossa nova](drums-bossa.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Other comping rhythms in the Latin group:** [Tango (habanera)](chords-tango.qmd), [Son montuno](chords-montuno.qmd), [Cha-cha](chords-chacha.qmd).
